subject: How to interpret abundance coefficients from gmultmix?

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: How to interpret abundance coefficients from gmultmix?
parts:
Hello,

In some cases, the summary of an unmarked model indicates the scale on which the regression coefficients (estimates) are provided. For example, see page 9 of the dynamic occupancy models vignette.

This doesn't seem to be the case for gmultmix. Here's part of my model summary:

Call:
gmultmix(lambdaformula = ~LAREA_0000 + REBU_0300 + REGS_0300, 
    phiformula = ~1, pformula = ~1, data = umfGMM, mixture = "NB")

Abundance:
            Estimate     SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    1.821 0.0305 59.77 0.00e+00
LAREA_0000     1.240 0.0245 50.66 0.00e+00
REBU_0300     -0.116 0.0231 -5.03 4.91e-07
REGS_0300     -0.103 0.0276 -3.74 1.84e-04

[truncated]

The scale of the regression coefficients (i.e., estimates) on abundance isn't indicated, so I don't know how to interpret (or transform) them.

I'd like to transform the above regression coefficients to their natural scale so I can interpret them in the usual way (i.e., a one unit change in X results in a beta change in abundance). Following an example in the unmarked overview,I tried this:

lc <- linearComb(AreaBurnHarv_nb, c(1,0,0,0), type="lambda") #intercept =1, all covariates = 0 (their mean)
backTransform(lc)

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Abundance estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept) LAREA_0000 REBU_0300 REGS_0300
     6.18 0.188    1.82           1          0         0         0

Transformation: exp 

...however this isn't resulting in coefficients on their natural scale, but (I think) abundance estimates when all covariates are set to the mean values. In other words, there are 6.18 critters when the covariates are at their mean.

I am obviously missing something, and would appreciate any help with transforming the betas to their natural scale.

Thanks,

Mark B.
Ph.D. Candidate
University of Saskatchewan

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: How to interpret abundance coefficients from gmultmix?
parts:
Hi Mark,

I'd suggest getting yourself a copy of the AHM book that Marc and Andy wrote.  This kind of material is covered there (and many other places), and it has less to do with unmarked than it does generalized linear modeling.  Your regression coefficients are not meaningful on a natural scale, aside from how they affect predictions of log-scale abundance which can themselves be back-transformed.  The gmultmix output for abundance is no different than any other Poisson or Negative Binomial regression.
